name_en: Hokki meshi — rice cooked in the broth of local surf clams
summary_ja: 醤油だれで煮たほっき貝のだしを米に吸わせて炊き、蒸らす際に貝を戻して混ぜ、しそを散らす相馬の一品。福島県唯一の潟湖・松川浦は明治期からほっき貝の名産地とされ、もとは漁師の船内食だったという。
summary_en: Rice is cooked in the broth of surf clams simmered in soy sauce, the clams folded back in as the rice steams and finished with shiso — a dish of Soma. Matsukawa-ura, Fukushima's only lagoon, has been known as a surf clam ground since the Meiji era, and the dish is said to have begun as food fishermen ate aboard their boats.
source_title: ほっきめし 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Harako meshi — rice piled high with soy-marinated salmon roe
summary_ja: 鮭から取り出したいくら（はらこ）の薄皮を丁寧に外し、酒と醤油に漬けて炊きたてのご飯にたっぷりのせる浜通りの料理。福島で最初に鮭の人工ふ化を取り入れたとされる請戸川流域の鮭漁とともに親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Salmon roe, its thin membrane carefully removed, is marinated in sake and soy sauce and piled thick over freshly cooked rice — a dish of the Hamadori coast. It is said to have grown up alongside the salmon fishery of the Ukedo River, where Fukushima's first salmon hatchery is said to have been built.
source_title: はらこ飯 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
